Code § 1950.6)","requirement":"A landlord or agent may charge an applicant a screening fee only to cover actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering information on the applicant (e.g., tenant screening or credit reporting service) plus the reasonable value of time spent. The fee may never exceed $30 per applicant, adjustable annually with the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. No fee may be charged when the landlord knows or should know no unit is available or will be available within a reasonable time. A fee may be charged only if the landlord offers either (A) first-complete-application-in-order processing under written screening criteria provided with the application, approval of the first qualifying applicant, and no charge unless the application is actually considered (inadvertent concurrent collections must be refunded within 7 days, or applied to another unit at the applicant's option), or (B) return of the entire fee to any applicant not selected within 7 days of selecting an applicant or 30 days of submission, whichever is first. The landlord must provide an itemized receipt (personally, by mail, or by agreed email), return any unused portion of the fee if no reference check or credit report is obtained, and give the applicant a copy of the credit report within 7 days of receiving it. Landlords may accept a reusable screening report under Section 1950.1.","key_value":"$30 per applicant maximum (CPI-adjustable since Jan. 1, 1998); refunds within 7 days","coverage_conditions":"Applies to landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants (including guarantors/cosignors) who request to rent a residential housing unit.","exemptions":"Does not preempt provisions or regulations governing the collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs. The fee is not an 'advance fee' under Bus. & Prof. Code § 10026 and is not 'security' under Civ.
